fix.value: The bhāṣya goes on: this store is therefore called 'of one life' (ekabhavika). One to be experienced in the seen birth starts a single ripening, as cause of experience, or a double one, as cause of life-span and experience, as with Nandīśvara or Nahuṣa. The mind, by contrast, has been variegated since beginningless time by latent tendencies (vāsanā) produced by the experience of afflictions, karma and ripening, spread out on all sides like a fishing net with its knots; these vāsanās go back over many lives, whereas the karma-store is of one life, and the impressions that cause memory are the vāsanās, which are beginningless. The one-life store is of fixed (niyata) or unfixed (aniyata) ripening, and the rule stated holds only for what is to be experienced in the seen birth with fixed ripening. Unfixed karma to be experienced in an unseen birth has three courses: what was done but has not ripened is destroyed (as the black is destroyed here by the arising of the white); or it merges (āvāpa-gamana) into a principal karma; or it remains long, overpowered by a principal karma of fixed ripening. Because the place, time and cause of its ripening cannot be ascertained, the course of karma is varied and hard to know; yet an exception does not cancel the general rule, so the one-life karma-store is accepted.

The excerpt in original is the first part of this long bhāṣya (the rice-grain simile; threefold ripening; the argument that a store made between two deaths produces one birth); the paraphrase also covers the rest of the bhāṣya (one-life store; fixed and unfixed ripening; the three courses of unfixed karma; latent tendencies from many lives). Vyāsa quotes a saying that two kinds of karma are to be known, one mass of the evil-doer's karma being destroyed by the meritorious, and another on a small admixture of demerit that does not outweigh much merit; both are given without a named source.

evidence: The paraphrase covered only the first part ('satsu kleśeṣu karmāśayo vipākārambhī ... tuṣāvanaddhāḥ śālitaṇḍulāḥ ... ekapraghaṭṭakena maraṇaṃ prasādhya ... trivipākaḥ'), which it renders faithfully, and left the bhāṣya's other main points to a note: 'ekabhavikaḥ karmāśayaḥ ... dṛṣṭajanmavedanīyas tv ekavipākārambhī ... dvivipākārambhī ... nandīśvaravan nahuṣavad vā ... vāsanābhir ... matsyajālaṃ granthibhir ivātatam ... niyatavipākaś cāniyatavipākaś ca ... trayī gatiḥ --- kṛtasyāvipakvasya nāśaḥ, pradhānakarmaṇy āvāpagamanaṃ vā ... ciram avasthānam ... karmagatiś citrā durvijñānā ... na cotsargasyāpavādān nivṛttiḥ'.
